entries.text: Welcome to the Getty Villa. It's past midnight and we are animals wandering the American Dream on the slippery edge of Western Civilization. My name is Ted Turner. I'm a media mogul. I am a sailor. And you are a friend of mine.I've invited you here to the Dream Getty, for no particular reason. You're free to roam around the grounds, talk with one another, and explore. As of now, we have the Library, the Galleria, and the Exedra. Over the next few weeks I'll be adding to the library. All of you are invited to share any sort of artwork or ideas in the Exedra. There will be a notebook in the exedra to discuss. As well, I'll be building an archive observatory somewhere on the mountain. So, besides being able to check out the art and communicate, there will be a few more activities and buildings to check out shortly. And besides all of that, I've actually built this place as a way to conceptualize the deeper dialectics of Prism. What's up on the graphmap is an early draft of the Iran conflict. That was early on in the parameters, we're much further now and I will be redrafting the Iran map over the next few weeks as I get ready to beta test Prism's closed form econometric system. You can check in periodically as I redraft the map, but I honestly hope the graphmap and Prism are just tangential to what you all might find here. All Prism could ever be is a sort of conceptual toy and I hope that by you all being here, filling this incredible space at this incredible time we can catch a vibe as the world spins into 2030 something.Oh, and if you're wondering why the Getty? It's the literal place where we can truly look back on thousands of years of human history and know that we actually have some clarity, that we can trust our Holy discernment. Joan said "[The Getty Villa teaches us] that we were never any better than we are, and will never be any better than we were"In gloria patria et filio et spiritu sancto sicut erat in principio et nunc et semper et in secula seculorum
